Metadata.title: Hyphae Consensus
Metadata.description: Hyphae Consensus portal: verifiable multi-agent reasoning and decision accountability.

App.name: Hyphae Consensus
App.tagline: Verifiable multi-agent reasoning and decision accountability
App.intro: Three AI roles (Proposer, Critic and Evidence Evaluator) work through a software-engineering problem. The runtime retrieves evidence from Hyphae memory and verifies its proofs, the Evaluator judges each claim against that evidence, and a fixed policy turns the result into a recommendation. Only a person can authorize it, and authorizing records a decision without executing anything.
App.buildNote: This build of the portal is not connected to the Hyphae Consensus API. It explains the system and shows the labels it will use; nothing in it calls a model or reads memory.

roles.title: Three roles deliberate
roles.body: The Proposer turns a task into explicit claims, the Critic challenges assumptions and risks, and the Proposer can revise.

evidence.title: The runtime checks evidence
evidence.body: The runtime, not a model, retrieves records from Hyphae memory and verifies their integrity proofs.

policy.title: A fixed policy recommends
policy.body: The Evidence Evaluator judges each claim against the evidence, and a deterministic policy turns those judgments and the proof statuses into a recommendation.

human.title: A person authorizes
human.body: Only a person can approve or reject. Approving records a decision; nothing is executed.

NewDeliberation.lead: Start a deliberation in one of two modes.

planned.guided: offer a guided example that starts instantly, with scripted roles and simulated evidence, labeled SIMULATED and calling no model;
planned.live: offer the curated presets of the Live Meta mode, which call Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot (presets only, no free text; runs of the final recorded battery took about 4 to 7 minutes);
planned.fallback: offer a recorded run instead when live mode is busy or its daily budget is used up;
planned.return: let you leave and come back to your run through My runs.

evidence.intro: Every record the runtime retrieved for this run: what its proof covers, its text, and how each proof was checked, round by round. Integrity, factual status and relevance are separate axes: a valid proof shows that a record matches what its proof sealed, not that the record is true, relevant or complete.

proofs.limitsHeading: What the receipt says proofs establish

limits.valid: A proof marked valid means that Hyphae’s verifier re-executed the request the proof sealed against its witness and accepted it at the anchor it was given (the pinned anchor wherever one is configured, always for the public snapshot).
limits.covers: It covers the whole result of that request (for the sealed snapshot, the complete record list of the snapshot’s project at that anchor), never a claim, even when the request’s query is a claim’s text, and a record’s text is not byte-compared with the proof.
limits.notEstablished: Proofs do not establish that the content is true, relevant or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.

audit.heading: Audit trail
audit.intro: The chain behind this run, its receipt, the verbatim log where it is published, and the command that checks a downloaded log against the receipt. The chain is unsigned SHA-256: it shows that records are consistent with a head obtained earlier, not that their content is true.
audit.partial: The server’s copy of this run could not be read: the links below come from the stream only.
audit.chainUnknown: The chain fields come with the server’s copy of the run, which has not been read.

scopes.run: This run’s records form a complete hash chain from genesis on their own: recomputing every record’s hash and link from them alone checks the run.
scopes.log: This run is one segment of a multi-run log: its records are linked to records of other runs, so checking its chain needs the whole log file, from its first line.
scopes.partly_chained: This run began before schema 1.1: its first records carry no hash chain, and the chain after them commits to them only by count.
scopes.unchained: Pre-1.1, unchained: these records carry no hash chain, so nothing in this run is tamper-evident and there is no head hash.

chain.heading: Check the chain in this browser
chain.intro: Downloads {name} and, for every record that carries a hash, recomputes its SHA-256 here from the line as written in the file, with only its hash value blanked. The runtime’s own check hashes instead its re-serialization of what it parses. On the canonical lines the runtime writes, the two give the same hash; on a line written any other way they give different hashes, so this check and the runtime’s can disagree in either direction: a record can check out here and fail the read-only command above, or the reverse. The check follows every link and compares this run’s records with the receipt and the detail.
chain.introUnchained: Downloads {name}, reads it as records in sequence with unique ids, and compares this run’s records with the file’s pinned digest (where there is one), the receipt and the detail. This run’s records carry no hash (pre-1.1), so there is no hash to recompute and no link to follow.
chain.introPartlyChained: Downloads {name} and reads it as records in sequence with unique ids. This run began before schema 1.1: its first records carry no hash, so for them there is no hash to recompute and no link to follow, and they are not chain-verified or tamper-evident. For every record of the file that carries a hash (this run’s later records among them), it recomputes its SHA-256 here from the line as written in the file, with only its hash value blanked, and follows its link. The runtime’s own check hashes instead its re-serialization of what it parses: on the canonical lines the runtime writes, the two give the same hash; on a line written any other way, they can disagree in either direction. The check compares this run’s records with the file’s pinned digest (where there is one), the receipt and the detail.
chain.unsupported: This browser offers no WebCrypto here (it needs a secure connection), so the chain cannot be checked in it.

What was checked: the file reads as records in sequence, with unique ids, and the comparisons marked below.} other {This run’s # records carry no hash (pre-1.1): no hash was recomputed and no link was followed, so nothing in them is chain-verified or tamper-evident. What was checked: the file reads as records in sequence, with unique ids, and the comparisons marked below.}}

chain.recordsLegacy: {chained, plural, =0 {No record of the file checked.} one {# record of the file checked: its hash recomputed, its link followed.} other {# records of the file checked: every hash recomputed, every link followed.}} {legacy, plural, =0 {Every record of the file carries a hash.} one {The # record before the chain carries no hash (pre-1.1) and is not chain-verified.} other {The # records before the chain carry no hash (pre-1.1) and are not chain-verified.}}

chain.head: Head of this run, the hash of its last record: {head}, against the receipt’s head.
chain.headNoReceipt: Head of this run, the hash of its last record: {head}; the receipt has not been read, so it is not compared.

chain.count: Record count against the receipt’s ({count, number}).
chain.countNoReceipt: The receipt has not been read, so the record count is not compared.
chain.limits: A chain that checks out shows that these bytes are consistent with each other and with the copies compared above. The chain is unsigned: a log rewritten and re-hashed as a whole would check out too, unless a digest obtained earlier (a manifest in a tagged commit, a receipt saved before) says otherwise; and it says nothing about whether the records are true. This check reads only the fields the chain is made of (schema version, sequence, event and run ids, link and hash): it does not check the rest of each record against the record format, does not replay the history and does not re-derive the recommendation, and it checks no content of a record without a hash (schema 1.0). The read-only command above also parses every record in full, replays the history and re-derives the recommendation. It is unsigned too and compares no pinned digest, so the same limit on a log rewritten and re-hashed as a whole applies to it.
chain.limitsUnchained: Without a chain, a record can be changed without leaving any trace inside the file: a SHA-256 that matches the digest the archive’s manifest pins shows only that these are the bytes archived, and only as far as that manifest is trusted. Nothing here is signed, and it says nothing about whether the records are true. This check reads only the fields the chain is made of (schema version, sequence, event and run ids, link and hash): it does not check the rest of each record against the record format and does not replay the history. The read-only command above also parses every record in full and replays the history, but without a chain it cannot show that the records are unchanged either.
chain.limitsUnchainedOwn: Without a chain, a record can be changed without leaving any trace inside the file, and this server’s log has no pinned digest to compare it with: nothing here shows that these are the records first written. Nothing here is signed, and it says nothing about whether the records are true. This check reads only the fields the chain is made of (schema version, sequence, event and run ids, link and hash): it does not check the rest of each record against the record format and does not replay the history. The read-only command above also parses every record in full and replays the history, but without a chain it cannot show that the records are unchanged either.

welcome.title: Welcome to Hyphae Consensus
welcome.body: Three AI roles work through a software-engineering problem, the runtime checks the evidence, and a fixed policy recommends. Only a person can authorize. In this build the portal is not connected, so its views say what they will do.

guided.title: Start with a guided example
guided.body: Once the portal is connected, a guided example will start instantly. Its roles will be scripted and its evidence simulated, so it will be labeled SIMULATED and will call no model.

live.title: Live Meta presets
live.body: Live runs will call Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0 on curated presets, with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot. Runs of the final recorded battery took about 4 to 7 minutes. When live mode is busy or its daily budget is used up, a recorded run will be offered instead.

runs.title: Come back through My runs
runs.body: A run will keep going if you close the page. You will find it again in My runs, where each run stays reachable for 24 hours.

labels.title: Read the labels
labels.body: Every run and event will say where it comes from: SIMULATED, LIVE META next to its evidence label, RECORDED or REPLAY. A valid proof shows that Hyphae can reproduce the sealed recall a record came from, not that the record is true.

decide.title: You decide, and nothing executes
decide.body: The recommendation comes from a deterministic policy, not from a vote. Approving records your decision only: no executor exists, and decisions made in the public portal carry no authority.

Provenance.heading: Provenance labels
Provenance.intro: Once connected, the portal will mark every run and event with where it comes from, on separate axes: the model (scripted or live Meta), the evidence (simulated or a sealed snapshot), the source (this server or the research archive) and the delivery of each event (live or replay). Labels will come from recorded data, never from the request. What they will mean:

simulated.label: SIMULATED
simulated.description: Simulated evidence: its proofs are not real. In guided runs the roles are scripted too and no model is called.

liveMeta.label: LIVE META
liveMeta.description: A run in progress: live calls to Meta’s muse-wonder-1.0, with evidence from a sealed Hyphae snapshot whose proofs are re-verified for every run. LIVE META never stands alone; the evidence label is always next to it.

metaModel.label: META MODEL
metaModel.description: Records of a run of Meta’s model shown afterwards (replayed, listed or archived): real model calls, but not happening now. LIVE META is shown only for records that arrive while you watch.

hybrid.description: A live model with simulated evidence: real model calls, but proofs that are not real. Some runs in the research archive are of this kind, and their labels say so.

recorded.label: RECORDED
recorded.description: A real run recorded earlier and shown from the research archive, not a run in progress. It keeps the model and evidence labels it was recorded with.

replay.label: REPLAY
replay.description: Stored events played back, not as they happen. A recorded run always plays as a replay.

flagNotes.provenance_inconsistent: The mode this run was declared with disagrees with what its records prove; it is never shown as live.
flagNotes.unchained: Records before schema 1.1 carry no hash chain.
flagNotes.mode_undeclared: The run was recorded before schema 1.3 and declares no mode.

Provenance.note: A valid proof shows that Hyphae can reproduce the sealed recall a record came from, not that the record is true, relevant or complete, or that a model used it.
